annotations.text:
Rebuilt from photographs of the city rather than from architectural theory.

The first five directions all inherited a "Bauhaus / White City" premise that was asserted early and never chosen — which is why they were all pale, flat and quiet. The real city is high-contrast and luminous: saturated turquoise water, deep cobalt dusk, warm amber light.

Same content in all three. Flip the Sunset toggle on each.

The photograph is real — Tel Aviv at blue hour by Martin Furtschegger, CC BY 3.0 via Wikimedia Commons, self-hosted and resized to 39KB. Attribution is printed in the artboard because the licence requires it.
Kept for the record. All five were rejected as not looking like Tel Aviv. The palette here is a desaturated version of the real thing — compare the sea colour against any photograph of the coast.
